items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 10, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So at that time I had to leave Barry Harris because he didn’t want to hear that in his house. “No Trane in my house.”

ctx.x: So the way he treated that language. I mean he had his own language. So at that time I had to leave Barry Harris because he didn’t want to hear that in his house. “No Trane in my house.” And I don’t want no Loony Tunes in my house. I said oh man, and Trane was hot at that time. Trane was — I mean every young musician wanted to play like that. We was playing Bird but here Trane came along. Trane came along. And that was the new sound. And this was like during Civil Rights, it was like the soundtrack of the…
all about emotions you know. And he was projecting that. And bebop is more like — bebop was more romantic. But Trane wasn’t in a romantic frame of mind with all these rights and stuff going on.
